bundle.author: danpelota
bundle.title: [DATA-2550] Use the adopted proposed maps as the only congressional and MI senate districts
bundle.body:
Supersedes #1180. [DATA-2550](https://app.clickup.com/t/86ajxyz) reported that FL-16 was missing from the office picker. The cause was that every seat moved to a 2026 map had no zip codes. Instead of filling zip codes for a separate district type, this PR makes the adopted proposed maps the only congressional and Michigan state senate districts.

## What changed

- **One swap:** `int__l2_nationwide_uniform` now writes the adopted proposed map into `US_Congressional_District` and `State_Senate_District`.
  - The gate is still `district_map_adoption` (proposed and verified, with the per-district narrowing). Virginia's struck-down map does not pass it.
  - Every consumer reads this view, so every model sees one map per type.
- **Removed:**
  - the `Congressional_District_2026` and `State_Senate_District_2026` types
  - `int__l2_proposed_district_aggregations`
  - the union code paths in `m_election_api__district`, `m_election_api__district_top_issues` and `int__icp_offices`
  - the turnout carry-over in `m_election_api__projected_turnout`
  - the two 2026 columns in `gp_api_voters`
  - the three tests that existed only for the 2026 types
- **Overrides:** the 219 rows in `l2_br_match_overrides` that pointed positions at the 2026 types are deleted. The matcher already maps all 219 positions to the same district number on `US_Congressional_District` (181) and `State_Senate_District` (38).
- **After 2026:** when L2 moves the new maps into its current columns and clears `Proposed_District`, the swap has nothing left to replace. No retirement step is needed.
- **Omni:** no change. Nothing in omni references the 2026 types. No stored record uses them either: campaigns, path to victory, organization overrides, voter file filters, outreach and polls were all checked.

## Verification (dev compared with prod)

- `int__l2_nationwide_uniform`, dev view compared with prod view:
  - Only `US_Congressional_District` changes, in FL, MO, NC and TX among the states sampled. Only `State_Senate_District` changes in MI.
  - VA and NY do not change. `State_House_District` does not change anywhere. No voter loses a value.
- Dev view compared with prod `gp_api_voters` 2026 columns:
  - The values match for every voter in AL, CA, FL, LA, MI, OH, TN and UT.
  - Small gaps in MO, NC and TX also appear in columns this PR does not touch, so they come from the monthly mart lagging fresh L2 loads.
- Built in dev:
  - Built: `int__icp_offices`, `m_election_api__district`, `m_election_api__projected_turnout`, `m_election_api__district_top_issues`, `m_election_api__position`, `m_people_api__district`, `int__zip_code_to_br_office`, `m_election_api__zip_to_position` and `m_election_api__race`.
  - All their tests pass, including `assert_race_projection_two_way_inference_parity` after a race rebuild.
  - One test fails, as expected: `relationships_m_people_api__districtvoter_district_id`. It fails on exactly the 95,928,678 prod district-voter rows of the two 2026 types (87,885,483 congressional and 8,043,195 MI senate). The cutover deletes them.

## Cutover (required before or with the first nightly after merge)

The view changes at once, but these incremental tables re-read a state only when its L2 file reloads. The adopted states last loaded between 2026-09-22 and 2026-10-02, so the next loads land too close to the November 3 election to wait for. Run this one-off backfill, in this order:

1. `int__l2_nationwide_uniform_w_haystaq`: update `US_Congressional_District` and `State_Senate_District` from the view for voters in the 11 adopted states.
2. `int__l2_district_aggregations`: recompute voter and phone counts for the adopted (state, type) districts.
3. `int__zip_code_to_l2_district`: `--full-refresh`. Its docstring already calls for periodic full refreshes to flush stale rows.
4. `gp_api_voters`: rebuild. It is a monthly full-rebuild table and takes about 5 hours.
5. `m_people_api__districtvoter`: delete the `Congressional_District_2026` and `State_Senate_District_2026` rows, and update the two types for voters in the adopted states.
6. People-db Postgres `DistrictVoter`: the 2026-type rows need clearing there as well. Door knocking reads from this table.

Until step 3 runs, FL-16 and the other seats show old-map zip codes in the picker. Until step 4 runs, their voter files use the old map.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core voter and district geography for adopted states across election API, ICP sizing, zip/office mapping, and district-voter links; production cutover backfills are required to avoid stale incremental data.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Adopted proposed redistricting maps are applied in-place** on the nationwide L2 uniform view: when `district_map_adoption` marks a state as proposed and verified, `US_Congressional_District` and `State_Senate_District` are overwritten from `Proposed_District` instead of minting parallel `*_2026` district types.
> 
> The PR **removes the parallel 2026 district model** (`int__l2_proposed_district_aggregations`), related macros (`proposed_district_minted_type`, `get_proposed_minted_district_types`), extra voter columns on `gp_api_voters`, unions in district/ICP/top-issues marts, and **turnout carry-over** from the old map onto minted districts. Downstream models now rely on a single map per type via `int__l2_district_aggregations` and standard district columns.
> 
> **219 `l2_br_match_overrides` rows** that pointed BallotReady positions at `Congressional_District_2026` / `State_Senate_District_2026` are deleted, along with tests that only guarded the minted-type path. Seed/docs wording shifts from “mint” to “adopt/replace.”
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 758e665ee0e763c4ca6783acc7bd785d2261fd5b. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

priorFindings.body:
**No test verifies that adopted maps actually propagate into output district columns.** The four deleted tests included `assert_adopted_states_mint_districts.sql`, which was self-described as "the only guard here that fails on absence rather than presence" — detecting if adoption rows in `district_map_adoption` actually produce district values downstream. The three surviving proposed-district tests (`assert_proposed_district_format`, `_no_drift`, `_seed_coverage`) only inspect the raw `Proposed_District` vendor column and seed presence; none reads `US_Congressional_District` or `State_Senate_District` from this model against `district_map_adoption` to verify the `adopted` CTE writes the proposed district number into those columns for voters in adopted states. A bug in this CTE (wrong join key, wrong CASE branch, wrong macro expansion) would leave all remaining tests green while silently leaving every adopted-state voter on the old map.

*(Falsification check: exhaustive search of `dbt/project/tests/*.sql` for references to `district_map_adoption`, `US_Congressional_District`, and `State_Senate_District` found no test that joins the output columns against the adoption seed to verify propagation.)*

**One-directional fan-out guard on `district_map_adoption` persists.** The new `expression_is_true` test (lines 890-900) rejects a per-district adoption row when a statewide row already exists for the same `(state, district_type)`, but a statewide row always passes because `nullif(trim(district_number), '') is null` is TRUE for it, short-circuiting the subquery check. If someone later adds per-district rows first and then inserts a statewide row, both pass all tests. In `int__l2_nationwide_uniform.sql` the LEFT JOIN's OR condition (`nullif(trim(adoption.district_number), '') is null OR cast(…) = cast(…)`) matches both rows for the same voter, duplicating their output. The `unique_combination_of_columns` test on `(state, district_type, district_number)` permits this because the two rows have different `district_number` values. The current seed has only statewide rows so the bug is latent, but the test gap allows a future committer to create the problematic combination without any CI failure.

Consider adding a symmetric guard that rejects a statewide row (`district_number IS NULL`) when per-district rows already exist for the same adopted+verified `(state, district_type)` scope.

*(Falsification check: no other constraint in seeds_schema.yaml or elsewhere guards against a statewide row coexisting with per-district rows for the same (state, district_type). Confirmed by reading the full seed schema and the JOIN logic.)*

findings.body:
**No test verifies that adopted maps actually propagate into output district columns.** The deleted `assert_adopted_states_mint_districts.sql` checked that adoption rows produced district values downstream (via `int__l2_proposed_district_aggregations`). That model is gone and the `adopted` CTE is its replacement, but no surviving test checks that, for a state in `district_map_adoption` with `adopted_source = 'proposed'` and `is_verified = true`, the output `US_Congressional_District` or `State_Senate_District` column actually contains the proposed district number rather than the original value. A join predicate mismatch (`adoption.district_type` vs. the macro-derived type, or a wrong `adopted_source` literal), or `is_verified` being uniformly false in the seed, would leave the `else` branch always taken — silently serving stale maps while `assert_proposed_district_seed_coverage` and `assert_proposed_district_format` both pass.

*(Falsification check: searched all 13 test files referencing `int__l2_nationwide_uniform` and all 3 referencing `district_map_adoption`; none perform a value-level check that the output district columns reflect the proposed number for adopted states.)*

**Voters with NULL or non-handled `Proposed_District` in adopted states silently keep the old-map district.** The `adopted` CTE's LEFT JOIN matches only when `proposed_district_type(voters.Proposed_District)` equals `adoption.district_type`. For voters whose `Proposed_District` is NULL or carries a non-handled value (county-commissioner, local annexation), the macro returns NULL, the join finds no match, and the CASE falls through to `else voters.US_Congressional_District` — preserving the pre-adoption district number. The file's comment at line 142 asserts "every consumer sees one map per type," but `assert_proposed_district_no_drift.sql` is explicitly scoped to `proposed_district is not null`, confirming nulls are expected. Unlike the prior approach (separate `Congressional_District_2026` column), the in-place replacement mixes old-map and new-map voters in a single column, so aggregations that group by congressional district in an adopted state will sum voters from two map vintages without any signal.

*(Falsification check: no test or documented guarantee ensures that `Proposed_District` is non-null and a handled shape for every voter in every adopted state; `assert_proposed_district_no_drift` explicitly filters to non-null rows.)*

output.summary: This PR replaces the parallel 2026 district types (`Congressional_District_2026`, `State_Senate_District_2026`) with in-place overwriting of `US_Congressional_District` and `State_Senate_District` via a new `adopted` CTE in `int__l2_nationwide_uniform`, driven by the `district_map_adoption` seed. It removes `int__l2_proposed_district_aggregations`, the union legs in five downstream marts, the 219 override rows that pointed at the 2026 types, the two voter-mart columns, and four tests that only guarded the minted-type path. The change matches the PR description well. The scout flagged three areas: (1) the incremental aggregation model not re-processing voters after a seed change — verified as an operational concern already documented in the PR's 6-step cutover; (2) voters in adopted states whose `Proposed_District` is NULL or a non-handled shape silently retaining their old-map district number, creating a mixed-map column — flagged at medium confidence because the prior approach kept the maps separate; (3) the deleted `assert_adopted_states_mint_districts` test has no replacement verifying that adopted district numbers actually reach the output columns — confirmed as a test gap (continues prior finding). The prior finding about one-directional fan-out guards on `district_map_adoption` is now fixed by the new symmetric test at lines 890–900 of `seeds_schema.yaml`. The human reviewer should confirm with the author that L2 populates `Proposed_District` for effectively all voters in adopted states so the mixed-map concern is moot, and should verify the 6-step cutover runs before or with the first nightly after merge.
